{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes (e.g., after 72+ peaks) by 5-15% to avoid overreaction.",
    "Adjust downward bias in forecasts when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 in recent days) — especially if price is trending upward.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2-5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "Increase downward bias when sentiment is neutral or negative and price is trending downward — especially if true outcome is below 65.00.",
    "Avoid over-optimism in early forecast windows (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) — use 3-day moving average to smooth initial predictions.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 3-7% to reflect underperformance.",
    "When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50 or above), allow slight upward bias but cap at +10% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Correct for lag: if true outcome is 2-3 days behind forecast, adjust forecast downward by 2-5% to reflect delayed market reaction."
  ]
}
